claims/a-rag-agent-formulates-its-own-re.description: RAG agent with retriever tool, query reformulation, HyDE, Self-Query, re-retrieval, smolagents ToolCallingAgent
claims/a-rag-agent-formulates-its-own-re.title: An agent armed with a retriever tool formulates its own retrieval query and critiques results to re-retrieve, naively recovering advanced RAG techniques like HyDE and Self-Query.

claims/a-relevance-grader-after-retrieva.description: document grading, relevance grader, conditional edge, binary score, corrective RAG, rewrite_question
claims/a-relevance-grader-after-retrieva.title: In the LangGraph agentic RAG design, an LLM grader gives a binary relevance score to retrieved documents and conditionally routes to answer generation if relevant or to question rewriting if not.

claims/a-small-model-can-typically-teach.description: DSPy teacher LM GPT-4o invoked few times for small student LM; teacher not strictly necessary, gives robustness to initial optimizer configuration.
claims/a-small-model-can-typically-teach.title: A small model can typically teach itself tasks like multi-hop retrieval in DSPy, with a larger teacher serving mainly as insurance against a poor initial configuration.

claims/a-tool-for-an-llm-agent-is-specif.description: tool definition, function calling, function schema, tool description, typed arguments, JSON schema parameters
claims/a-tool-for-an-llm-agent-is-specif.title: A tool for an LLM agent is essentially a function, specified to the model by a textual description of what it does and its arguments, preferably with types.

claims/a-unified-tool-server-framework-r.description: VerlTool competitive performance math search SQL visual reasoning SWE GAIA unified framework
claims/a-unified-tool-server-framework-r.title: Models trained in one unified framework (VERLTOOL) match or exceed task-specific agentic RL baselines across six tool-use domains, e.g. 45.9% average on knowledge QA versus Search-R1.

claims/action-level-penalties-for-missin.description: F1+ reward, action-level penalty, no search penalty, no answer penalty, reward shaping, stability, deep research agent
claims/action-level-penalties-for-missin.title: Adding small penalties for omitting the search or answer action to the F1 reward removes the answer-refusal collapse and lets F1-based training surpass the EM baseline.

claims/agent-baselines-uses-one-uv-sub-p.description: per-solver uv sub-projects, lockfiles, dependency isolation, inspect_ai version conflicts, reproducibility, agent-baselines
claims/agent-baselines-uses-one-uv-sub-p.title: The agent-baselines repo gives each solver its own uv sub-project and lockfile to avoid cross-solver dependency conflicts (notably inspect_ai versions) and to make runs reproducible per solver.

claims/agentic-rag-scored-86-9-percent-v.description: agentic RAG vs standard RAG evaluation, LLM judge, 86.9% vs 73.1%, no-knowledge-base baseline 36%, huggingface_doc_qa_eval
claims/agentic-rag-scored-86-9-percent-v.title: On an LLM-judged QA set over Hugging Face documentation, agentic RAG scored 86.9% versus 73.1% for standard RAG, and an LLM without the knowledge base scored 36%.

claims/ai-geometry-prover-relies-on-synt.description: AI olympiad geometry proof system, ~100 million synthetic proofs, symbolic logic deduction engine, LLM contribution limited, AlphaGeometry critique
claims/ai-geometry-prover-relies-on-synt.title: The highlighted AI geometry prover was trained on about 100 million synthetically generated proofs of a narrow kind and relies heavily on a decades-old non-LLM symbolic engine.

claims/an-unoptimized-two-module-multi-h.description: DSPy multi-hop retrieval baseline, Hop module, query generation plus note appending, BM25S over Wikipedia 2017 abstracts, HoVer 3-hop, top-5 recall about 31% with Llama-3.1-8B.
claims/an-unoptimized-two-module-multi-h.title: An unoptimized two-module multi-hop retrieval program on Llama-3.1-8B reaches only about 31% top-5 recall on 3-hop HoVer claims.

claims/asta-scholarqa-and-paper-finder-b.description: Asta ScholarQA SQA, Asta Paper Finder, production systems, Asta Summarize Literature, Asta Find Papers, retrieval and reranking
claims/asta-scholarqa-and-paper-finder-b.title: The Asta ScholarQA and Asta Paper Finder baselines are variants of the production systems behind Asta Summarize Literature and Asta Find Papers respectively.

claims/asta-v0-routes-each-task-to-a-spe.description: Asta-v0 router agent, task-type detection, dispatch to specialized sub-agents, orchestrator, AstaBench
claims/asta-v0-routes-each-task-to-a-spe.title: Asta-v0 is a routing agent that dispatches each task to a specialized agent based on the detected task type.

claims/astabench-0-5-2-pins-inspect-ai-0.description: astabench version pin, inspect_ai 0.3.114, Inspect AstaBench coupling, override-dependencies
claims/astabench-0-5-2-pins-inspect-ai-0.title: astabench 0.5.2 pins inspect_ai 0.3.114, and solvers that need a different version must use uv override-dependencies.

claims/astabench-coding-tasks-require-th.description: AstaBench SUPER, CORE-bench, DiscoveryBench, python_session tool, SandboxJupyter, sandbox files, trajectory tracking, scoring requirements
claims/astabench-coding-tasks-require-th.title: AstaBench coding and data tasks may require the provided sandbox and stateful python_session tool for accurate scores: SUPER tracks trajectories through it, CORE-bench scores a result file written in the sandbox, and DiscoveryBench reads files from the sandbox.

claims/astabench-decouples-solve-and-sco.description: eval_then_score.sh, decoupled solve score, cross-version inspect_ai, frozen scorer project solvers/scorer, --no-score
claims/astabench-decouples-solve-and-sco.title: For solvers that cannot share astabench's inspect_ai version, AstaBench offers a decoupled flow that solves with --no-score and then scores in a separately pinned scorer project.

claims/astabench-eval-records-the-git-sh.description: astabench eval reproducibility, git sha in logs, uncommitted changes, --ignore-git, wrapper around inspect eval-set, --split
claims/astabench-eval-records-the-git-sh.title: astabench eval, a wrapper around inspect eval-set, records the git sha in logs and fails on uncommitted changes unless --ignore-git is set.

claims/astabench-leaderboard-classifies-.description: AstaBench leaderboard submission, toolset categories Standard Custom Interface Custom, openness categories open source open weights closed API UI
claims/astabench-leaderboard-classifies-.title: AstaBench leaderboard submissions are classified by tool usage (Standard, Custom Interface, Custom) and by openness (open/closed source and weights, API-only, UI-only).

claims/astabench-literature-search-tools.description: AstaBench literature tasks, standardized search tools, date restriction, corpus restriction, rubric validity, alternative search tools lower scores
claims/astabench-literature-search-tools.title: AstaBench literature tasks provide search tools with date and corpus restrictions so task rubrics stay valid as new papers are published, and using alternative search tools may lower scores.

claims/astabench-max-samples-should-not-.description: AstaBench parallelism, --max-samples, CPU cores, asyncio.to_thread ThreadPool deadlock, INSPECT_DOCKER_CLI_CONCURRENCY 2N, ASTA_TOOL_KEY rate limit 8 samples
claims/astabench-max-samples-should-not-.title: AstaBench advises --max-samples no greater than CPU cores (about 8 for literature tasks, saturating the ~4 req/s Asta tool rate limit) and INSPECT_DOCKER_CLI_CONCURRENCY of at least twice that, to avoid deadlocks.

claims/astabench-measures-solver-cost-as.description: AstaBench cost logging, accuracy and cost, model usage tracking, record_model_usage_with_inspect, bridge, AsyncOpenAI
claims/astabench-measures-solver-cost-as.title: AstaBench measures a solver's cost as well as its accuracy, so solvers must ensure all model usage is logged (automatically via InspectAI model calls, or manually with record_model_usage_with_inspect).

claims/astabench-provides-over-2400-exam.description: AstaBench size, 2400 examples, 11 benchmarks, literature search, code execution, data analysis, end-to-end discovery
claims/astabench-provides-over-2400-exam.title: AstaBench provides over 2,400 examples across 11 benchmarks spanning literature search, code execution, data analysis and end-to-end discovery.

claims/asynchronous-per-trajectory-rollo.description: async rollout, synchronous batch, tool call latency, GPU idle bubbles, speedup, VerlTool agentic RL
claims/asynchronous-per-trajectory-rollo.title: Letting each trajectory call the tool server independently (asynchronous rollout) instead of batch-synchronously speeds up rollouts by about 1.2x to 2x depending on the task.

claims/attention-dilution-drives-the-gol.description: attention dilution, softmax dilution, softmax denominator, gold document attention mass 0.91 to 0.01, layer 19, long context retrieval failure
claims/attention-dilution-drives-the-gol.title: As the in-context corpus grows, irrelevant documents dominate the softmax denominator and the gold document's share of attention output collapses (0.91 to 0.01 at layer 19).

claims/blocksearch-adds-an-on-policy-aux.description: on-policy auxiliary loss, exposure bias, teacher forcing, rolled-out digit prefixes, document identifier codes, BlockSearch training
claims/blocksearch-adds-an-on-policy-aux.title: BlockSearch adds an on-policy auxiliary loss over the model's own rolled-out identifier-digit prefixes because teacher forcing alone causes exposure bias.

claims/blocksearch-in-context-retrieval-.description: BlockSearch length generalization failure, recall near zero at million-token context, worse than dense retrieval, extrapolation collapse
claims/blocksearch-in-context-retrieval-.title: Without attention modifications, BlockSearch recall approaches zero near million-token corpora, far below a simple dense retrieval baseline.

claims/blocksearch-matches-a-same-backbo.description: BlockSearch 0.6B in-context retriever vs dense retriever, Recall@1 95.8 vs 95.5, MS MARCO 45k tokens, small corpus parity
claims/blocksearch-matches-a-same-backbo.title: BlockSearch matches a same-backbone dense retriever on small corpora, reaching 95.8% vs 95.5% Recall@1 on MS MARCO at about 45k tokens.

claims/chemcrow-pauses-generation-after-.description: ChemCrow ReAct format, Thought Action Action Input Observation, generation pauses, tool execution, iterative loop until final answer
claims/chemcrow-pauses-generation-after-.title: In ChemCrow, after the LLM emits an Action and Action Input, text generation pauses, the program executes the requested tool, and the result is returned prepended by 'Observation' before the next Thought, iterating until a final answer.

claims/clin-improves-on-repeated-task-at.description: CLIN, continual learning agent, reflection, memory of lessons, rapid task adaptation, self-improvement across trials
claims/clin-improves-on-repeated-task-at.title: CLIN agents reflect on each attempt at a task and store lessons in memory, so performance improves the more times the task is tried.

claims/deep-dxsearch-assistance-raised-p.description: Deep-DxSearch physician-in-the-loop study, clinician diagnostic accuracy assisted vs unassisted, 150 real cases, medical agentic RAG
claims/deep-dxsearch-assistance-raised-p.title: In a validation on 150 real-world cases, Deep-DxSearch assistance raised physicians' average diagnostic accuracy from 45.6% to 69.1%.

claims/deep-dxsearch-outperforms-standar.description: Deep-DxSearch agentic RL vs training-free standard RAG, diagnosis accuracy, in-distribution ID, out-of-distribution OOD margins
claims/deep-dxsearch-outperforms-standar.title: Deep-DxSearch's agentic RL strategy surpassed standard RAG approaches by 29.7% on in-distribution and 9.7% on out-of-distribution diagnosis data.

claims/dvc-repro-does-not-rerun-a-stage-.description: dvc repro caching, stale eval results, force rerun, score_sqa --force --downstream, dvc.lock hash, SQA release runs
claims/dvc-repro-does-not-rerun-a-stage-.title: In the agent-baselines SQA dvc pipeline, a code change to a solver or scorer that leaves the stage cmd unchanged does not trigger a rerun, so the stage must be forced (e.g. with --force --downstream).

claims/existing-medical-rag-systems-perf.description: medical RAG limitation, static heuristic one-shot retrieval, no adaptive re-query, irrelevant or conflicting evidence
claims/existing-medical-rag-systems-perf.title: Existing medical RAG systems typically perform static one-shot retrieval on the initial query and fail to adapt when retrieved evidence is insufficient, irrelevant or conflicting.

claims/f1-reward-training-collapses-thro.description: F1 vs exact match EM reward, answer avoidance, answer rate drop, outcome reward, training collapse, deep research RL
claims/f1-reward-training-collapses-thro.title: Training a search agent with an F1 outcome reward collapses through answer avoidance and ends below EM-reward training, because withholding an answer earns the same zero reward as a wrong answer.

claims/fast-thinking-prompt-template-tra.description: Fast Thinking vs Slow Thinking prompt template, think tags, Search-R1, deep research RL stability, accuracy
claims/fast-thinking-prompt-template-tra.title: In Search-R1 RL training, a Fast Thinking template that outputs search and answer decisions directly trains more stably and scores higher than the Slow Thinking template with explicit think tags.

claims/grpo-converges-faster-than-ppo-in.description: PPO vs GRPO, convergence speed, reward collapse, training stability, critic warm-up, Search-R1
claims/grpo-converges-faster-than-ppo-in.title: In Search-R1 training, GRPO converges faster than PPO but can suffer reward collapse after many steps, while PPO stays stable and both reach comparable final reward.

claims/in-the-ai-geometry-proof-only-2-o.description: AI proof vs human proof, >100 deductive steps, only 2 steps from LLM, rest from symbolic engine, elegance creativity
claims/in-the-ai-geometry-proof-only-2-o.title: In the AI-generated geometry proof shown, over 100 technical deductive steps were needed and only 2 came from the LLM, the rest from the symbolic engine, whereas the human proof is short.

claims/individual-attention-heads-locate.description: retrieval heads, per-head gold document ranking, attention heads vs decoded answer, latent retrieval signal, degrades with corpus size
claims/individual-attention-heads-locate.title: Individual attention heads rank the gold document first more often than the model decodes it, though this signal also weakens as corpus size grows.

claims/joint-prompt-optimization-with-mi.description: MIPROv2 jointly optimizing the query-generation and note-appending prompts, GPT-4o teacher, Llama-3.1-8B, top5_recall 31% to 59%, about 35 minutes and 5 dollars.
claims/joint-prompt-optimization-with-mi.title: Jointly optimizing the two prompts of a multi-hop retrieval program with MIPROv2 roughly doubles top-5 recall from about 31% to about 59%.

claims/large-and-evolving-tool-pools-wit.description: tool retrieval, large tool pool, complex tool docs, evolving APIs, tool selection scaling
claims/large-and-evolving-tool-pools-wit.title: Complex tool documentation and huge, constantly evolving tool pools motivate retrieving relevant tools rather than putting all of them in context.

claims/length-aware-softmax-and-document.description: length-aware softmax plus document-level sparse attention routing, MS MARCO million-token Recall@1 0.2 to 20.0, dense baseline 20.2
claims/length-aware-softmax-and-document.title: Length-aware softmax scaling plus document-level sparse attention raise million-token Recall@1 on MS MARCO from 0.2 to 20.0, close to the dense baseline's 20.2.

claims/literature-based-discovery-uses-t.description: Literature-based discovery LBD, Don Swanson 1986, ABC paradigm, A-B B-C infer A-C, hypothesis generation from literature
claims/literature-based-discovery-uses-t.title: Literature-based discovery (Swanson, 1986) generates new hypotheses from the literature via the ABC paradigm: if A relates to B and B relates to C, propose a link between A and C.

claims/llm-generated-scientific-ideas-ar.description: LLM idea generation failure modes, generic suggestions, copied details, simple logical modification, buzz concepts, novelty boosting combinations
claims/llm-generated-scientific-ideas-ar.title: LLM-generated scientific ideas are often generic suggestions woven with details copied from the context or simple logical modifications of it, and novelty boosting tends to add combinations of buzz concepts.

claims/llms-generate-scientific-directio.description: LLM scientific idea generation, hypothesis generation, lack of novelty creativity, SciMON ACL 2024, Tom Hope experiments
claims/llms-generate-scientific-directio.title: In the author's experiments on scientific idea generation (SciMON), LLMs generate research directions that lack novelty and creativity.

claims/log-n-scaled-softmax-helps-in-con.description: SSMax, scalable softmax, log N scaling of pre-softmax scores, attention sink, length-aware softmax, mitigation of attention dilution
claims/log-n-scaled-softmax-helps-in-con.title: Scaling pre-softmax scores with log N (SSMax) is effective against attention dilution, whereas an additive length-aware attention sink barely helps.

claims/marg-uses-multiple-llm-agents-eac.description: MARG multi-agent review generation, scientific paper review, critique and enhance ideas, multiple LLM agents, aspects
claims/marg-uses-multiple-llm-agents-eac.title: MARG (2024) generates reviews of scientific papers using multiple LLM agents, each focusing on reviewing different aspects.

claims/modified-blocksearch-beats-dense-.description: LIMIT benchmark, out-of-distribution lexical retrieval, in-context retrieval beats dense embeddings, Recall@1 13.5 vs 2.9
claims/modified-blocksearch-beats-dense-.title: On the lexical LIMIT benchmark at a million-token corpus, modified BlockSearch reaches 13.5% Recall@1 versus 2.9% for the dense baseline.

claims/optimized-query-generator-decompo.description: Optimized DSPy hop query generator with empty notes issues a sub-question for the missing bridge entity (author of Up Against It), query decomposition per hop.
claims/optimized-query-generator-decompo.title: With empty notes, the optimized hop query generator asks only for the first missing bridge entity of a multi-hop claim rather than querying the whole claim.

claims/over-one-million-biomedical-paper.description: biomedical literature volume, publication rate, explosion of science, >1M papers per year
claims/over-one-million-biomedical-paper.title: More than one million biomedical papers are published every year.

claims/process-based-reward-co-optimizin.description: Deep-DxSearch ablation, process reward, soft verifiable reward for retrieval and reasoning vs outcome-only target reward, diagnosis accuracy
claims/process-based-reward-co-optimizin.title: In Deep-DxSearch ablations, a process-based reward that jointly optimizes retrieval and reasoning yields a 13.7% accuracy gain over target-only supervision.

claims/reinforce-outperforms-ppo-and-grp.description: REINFORCE vs PPO vs GRPO, policy optimization comparison, stability, search action count, Search-R1, deep research
claims/reinforce-outperforms-ppo-and-grp.title: In Search-R1 training, REINFORCE reaches better accuracy than PPO and GRPO with fewer search actions, while GRPO is the least stable of the three.

claims/research-beats-iterative-rag-base.description: ReSearch results, multi-hop QA, HotpotQA 2Wiki MuSiQue Bamboogle, exact match, LLM-as-judge, IRCoT, Iter-RetGen baselines
claims/research-beats-iterative-rag-base.title: ReSearch improves over the best prompt-based multi-step RAG baseline by an average of 15.81% EM and 17.56% LLM-as-judge at 7B, and 14.82% EM and 15.46% LLM-as-judge at 32B.

claims/research-masks-retrieval-result-t.description: retrieval result masking, loss masking, observation tokens, GRPO, ReSearch, search environment tokens
claims/research-masks-retrieval-result-t.title: ReSearch masks retrieved result tokens from the GRPO loss so that only thinking and search-query tokens generated by the policy are optimized.

claims/research-reward-is-answer-f1-with.description: ReSearch reward function, F1 answer reward, format reward 0.1, rule-based reward, boxed answer, reward shaping
claims/research-reward-is-answer-f1-with.title: ReSearch uses a rule-based reward equal to the answer F1 score, with 0.1 for a zero-F1 rollout in correct format and 0 otherwise.

claims/research-rl-elicits-reflection-an.description: emergent reflection, self-correction, query reformulation after bad search results, RL elicited behavior, ReSearch case study
claims/research-rl-elicits-reflection-an.title: ReSearch RL training elicits reflection and self-correction, such as reformulating a failed search query, without pre-defined heuristics.

claims/research-trained-only-on-musique-.description: generalization, single training set MuSiQue, transfer to HotpotQA 2WikiMultiHopQA Bamboogle, ReSearch
claims/research-trained-only-on-musique-.title: ReSearch models trained only on the MuSiQue training set generalize to other multi-hop QA benchmarks with different question types.

claims/research-trains-llms-to-interleav.description: ReSearch framework, reasoning with search, GRPO, no SFT, think/search/result tags, multi-hop RAG, Qwen2.5
claims/research-trains-llms-to-interleav.title: ReSearch trains LLMs with GRPO to interleave text-based thinking and search queries in one reasoning chain, without any supervised data on reasoning steps.

claims/retrieved-text-should-be-treated-.description: prompt injection defense, retrieved context as data, grader prompt, generator prompt, RAG security
claims/retrieved-text-should-be-treated-.title: The LangGraph agentic RAG tutorial instructs both the grader and the answer generator to treat retrieved documents as data only and ignore instructions inside them.

claims/rewriting-the-question-and-retryi.description: query rewriting, retry loop, retrieval failure recovery, hallucination avoidance, agentic RAG
claims/rewriting-the-question-and-retryi.title: A rewrite-and-retry loop that returns control to the query-generation node lets a RAG agent recover from a weak first retrieval instead of stopping or hallucinating an answer.

claims/rl-from-instruction-tuned-models-.description: base vs instruction-tuned initialization, RL from scratch, Qwen2.5 7B 32B, ReSearch, starting checkpoint
claims/rl-from-instruction-tuned-models-.title: In ReSearch, RL training starting from instruction-tuned models gives higher performance than starting from base models, consistently across benchmarks and model sizes.

claims/scideator-novelty-checking-retrie.description: Scideator novelty checker, Semantic Scholar search API, Specter embeddings, RankGPT reranking, top N papers, novelty classification and reasoning
claims/scideator-novelty-checking-retrie.title: Scideator's novelty evaluation collects candidate papers via the Semantic Scholar search API, filters them with Specter embeddings and RankGPT re-ranking, and classifies the idea's novelty against the most relevant papers.

claims/scideator-recombines-purpose-and-.description: Scideator, human-LLM idea generation, paper facet recombination, purpose mechanism, analogous papers, novelty classification
claims/scideator-recombines-purpose-and-.title: Scideator extracts purpose and mechanism facets from user-provided and analogous papers, recombines selected facets into ideas with one purpose and one mechanism, and classifies ideas as novel or not novel with a reason.

claims/scimon-augmentations-improved-ide.description: SciMON results, higher technical detail, less generic, perceived novelty utility, still insufficient novelty
claims/scimon-augmentations-improved-ide.title: SciMON's modelling augmentations yielded more technically detailed, less generic ideas with higher perceived novelty and utility, but the directions were still judged far from sufficient in novelty and utility.

claims/scimon-iterative-novelty-boosting.description: SciMON retrieve-compare-update, iterative novelty boosting at inference, similarity threshold, related work retrieval, novelty penalty
claims/scimon-iterative-novelty-boosting.title: SciMON boosts novelty at inference with a retrieve-compare-update loop that retrieves related work and instructs the model to update the idea in light of it and the initial problem.

claims/scimon-novelty-boosting-gives-a-1.description: SciMON novelty boosting evaluation, human expert ratings, CS biomedical experts, 1.5x 2x vs GPT-4 ideas
claims/scimon-novelty-boosting-gives-a-1.title: In human evaluations by CS and biomedical experts, SciMON novelty boosting gave a 1.5X-2X boost over GPT-4 idea ratings.

claims/search-call-count-and-response-le.description: number of search operations, response length, training dynamics, tool call growth, ReSearch, multi-hop
claims/search-call-count-and-response-le.title: During ReSearch RL training, the average number of search operations per rollout grows consistently and response length generally increases.

claims/search-r1-improves-over-rag-basel.description: Search-R1 main results, average relative improvement, RAG baselines, seven QA datasets, Qwen2.5-7B 3B, EM
claims/search-r1-improves-over-rag-basel.title: Search-R1 achieves 24% (Qwen2.5-7B) and 20% (Qwen2.5-3B) average relative improvement over RAG baselines across seven QA datasets.

claims/search-r1-instruct-models-converg.description: base vs instruct initialization, convergence speed, final reward parity, Qwen2.5 3B 7B, Search-R1, RL closes gap
claims/search-r1-instruct-models-converg.title: In Search-R1, instruction-tuned models converge faster and start higher than base models, but final training reward of both is highly similar.

claims/search-r1-plus-plus-raises-search.description: Search-R1++ baseline, Fast Thinking, REINFORCE, F1+ reward, Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen2.5-3B, QA benchmarks
claims/search-r1-plus-plus-raises-search.title: Search-R1++, combining the Fast Thinking template, REINFORCE and penalty-augmented F1 reward, raises Search-R1 average accuracy from 0.403 to 0.442 on Qwen2.5-7B and from 0.289 to 0.331 on Qwen2.5-3B.

claims/search-r1-response-length-first-d.description: response length dynamics, decrease-increase-stabilize, valid search calls grow, training dynamics, Search-R1 Qwen2.5-7B base
claims/search-r1-response-length-first-d.title: During Search-R1 training on Qwen2.5-7B base, response length first drops sharply for about 100 steps and then rises as the model learns to call search more often.

claims/search-r1-retrieved-token-loss-ma.description: retrieved token loss masking ablation, observation masking, Search-R1, PPO, Qwen2.5-7B base, EM 0.431 vs 0.343
claims/search-r1-retrieved-token-loss-ma.title: In Search-R1 with PPO on Qwen2.5-7B base, masking retrieved tokens from the loss raises average EM over seven QA datasets from 0.343 to 0.431.

claims/search-r1-uses-an-exact-match-out.description: outcome-based reward, exact match EM reward, no format reward, no neural reward model, rule-based, Search-R1
claims/search-r1-uses-an-exact-match-out.title: Search-R1 trains with a rule-based outcome reward equal to exact match of the final answer, without format rewards or a neural reward model.

claims/sft-improves-in-distribution-diag.description: supervised fine-tuning SFT vs reinforcement learning RL generalization, memorization, rare disease OOD cohort Xinhua-Rare, Deep-DxSearch
claims/sft-improves-in-distribution-diag.title: For diagnosis, SFT improves in-distribution performance but often degrades on out-of-distribution cohorts, whereas agentic RL training learns a transferable policy.

claims/slow-thinking-training-collapse-c.description: Slow Thinking collapse, empty think blocks, reasoning length growth, credit assignment shortcut, PPO, Search-R1
claims/slow-thinking-training-collapse-c.title: Training collapse under the Slow Thinking template coincides with a surge of empty think blocks, whose count correlates positively with reward just before collapse.

claims/the-first-scientific-journal-appe.description: history of scientific publishing, first scientific journal 1665, before journals self-published books and letters
claims/the-first-scientific-journal-appe.title: The first scientific journal appeared in 1665; until the mid-17th century science was communicated through self-published books and letters.

claims/the-model-deciding-whether-to-cal.description: agentic RAG, retriever as tool, bind_tools, model decides to retrieve or answer directly, LangGraph
claims/the-model-deciding-whether-to-cal.title: Letting the model decide whether to call the retriever tool, instead of always retrieving, is what makes a RAG system agentic rather than a fixed retrieve-then-generate pipeline.

claims/the-retriever-tool-prompt-tells-t.description: retriever tool description, affirmative-form queries not questions, multiple diverse queries, prompt engineering for agentic RAG
claims/the-retriever-tool-prompt-tells-t.title: The Hugging Face agentic RAG cookbook instructs the agent to write retrieval queries as affirmative sentences rather than questions and to call the retriever several times with semantically different queries.

claims/tokenizing-actions-and-observatio.description: tokenization, concatenation, token prefix consistency, on-policy, multi-turn rollout, Qwen2.5 tokenizer
claims/tokenizing-actions-and-observatio.title: Tokenizing LLM action strings and tool observation strings separately and appending token lists avoids boundary-merging mismatches that joint tokenization of the concatenated string can cause.

claims/tool-call-frequency-during-rl-fal.description: SQL fewer tool calls, DeepSearch more tool calls, memorization, tool utility, agentic RL dynamics
claims/tool-call-frequency-during-rl-fal.title: During RL training, tool call counts fall when tool outputs can be memorized (SQL execution results) and rise when they cannot (information-rich search results).

claims/tool-observation-tokens-are-off-p.description: observation tokens, off-policy, loss masking, GRPO, multi-turn tool use RL, training stability
claims/tool-observation-tokens-are-off-p.title: In agentic RL with tool use, tool observation tokens are off-policy for the policy being optimized and are therefore masked out of the policy-optimization loss.

claims/tool-use-vanishes-during-rl-witho.description: tool call frequency collapse, reward design, initialization, agentic RL, visual reasoning
claims/tool-use-vanishes-during-rl-witho.title: Models do not spontaneously develop effective tool use in RL without appropriate reward design, and tool action frequency can decay to zero within a few RL steps.
